qc.label_under_test: a preposition right after an abstract framing noun it idiomatically pairs with, opening a 'which' clause (the mechanism by, the grounds on, the setting in, the terms under; strongest with ' by'); quiet after concrete nouns (the cupboard in, the lamp by) and in passive or travel 'by' (written by, went by bus)

neighbours.label: a preposition right after an abstract framing noun it idiomatically pairs with, opening a 'which' clause (the mechanism by, the grounds on, the setting in, the terms under; strongest with ' by'); quiet after concrete nouns (the cupboard in, the lamp by) and in passive or travel 'by' (written by, went by bus)
fire: Doctors still debate the pathway by which the virus spreads.
Nobody knows the exact means by which it entered the cell.
She studied the manner in which children learn to read.
This explains the rate at which the glacier melts.
We reviewed the basis on which the award was made.
They traced the channels through which the funds moved.
It describes the way in which birds find their nests.
He questioned the procedure by which judges are chosen.
quiet: Doctors still read the novel by Dickens on the ward.
Nobody saw the small boat by the river at dawn.
She studied the map in the kitchen before she left.
This explains the sign at the end of the road.
We reviewed the book on the table last week.
They walked the dog through the park before lunch.
It describes the house in the woods behind the farm.
He questioned the man by the door about the keys.

notes: QC confirm, no probing; only the card was read. Fire uses frames with several framing nouns and prepositions; near misses keep the same prepositions after nouns that don't take a 'which' clause. The model can't see 'which', so the reading has to come from the noun.
